podcast.title: Three tiny tomatoes

hosts.Leyla: lives in Baku and loves a good plan
hosts.Sam: grew up in Manchester and once travelled with no plan at all

before.predict: Do you know where your food comes from? Guess: where did Sam spend last weekend?

lines.t: Hi everyone, and welcome to the SpeakLab Podcast. I'm Leyla.
And I'm Sam. Today's topic is farming and where our food comes from. And I spent last weekend on a farm!
At my uncle's place in Guba?
Yes! The apple harvest. Two days of picking apples from morning to evening.
Guba apples are famous. Were you tired?
My arms hurt more than my legs after a race. But the apples were amazing.
My uncle says it was a good year. Last year there was a drought — no rain for two months.
What happened to the crop?
They lost almost half of it. Farmers are always fighting the weather.
Your uncle doesn't use chemicals, does he?
No, everything is organic. He says good soil is the most important thing on a farm.
He's so calm and kind. Very down to earth.
That's rural life. Early to bed, early to rise. No traffic, no deadlines.
Except the weather. On Saturday it looked like rain, so we worked until dark.
Make hay while the sun shines, as they say.
Exactly. And now I'm trying to grow tomatoes on my balcony.
How's it going?
Three tomatoes in two months. [laugh] Very small ones.
Well, you reap what you sow. Maybe give them more water and sun.
And more love. I talk to them every morning.
Here's your question for your next SpeakLab call: do you know where your food comes from — and could you live on a farm?
I could. For two days. See you next time!
Bye for now!
